column1: # The geometry fixtures the service queries, one row per profile. A request
# names a profile_id and a ray count and nothing else the query reads: the
# scene, the query set, and the device belong to the row, so a caller chooses
# among fixtures and supplies no geometry, native code, path, or OptiX or CUDA
# flag. The service validates the ledger whole before it answers a request,
# the way physics-profiles.tsv is read.
# profile_id       the name a request carries
# scene            the fixture the runtime builds; the runtime refuses a name it
#                  does not carry
# query_set        the ray set the runtime generates from the count
# max_rays         the ceiling a request's rays is bounded by
# timeout_s        the service's deadline for one job
# execution_policy refused or validator-gated, the same reading the web,
#                  image, and physics ledgers give the field: refused emits
#                  no tool
# device_index     the CUDA device the runtime binds
# module_cache     enabled or disabled, the OptiX disk cache available to
#                  optixModuleCreate. optix_host.h states there is no
#                  in-memory cache, so the module stage either compiles the
#                  PTX or reads a compiled module back, and a cold-start
#                  timing that does not pin this measures run history. The
#                  service sets OPTIX_CACHE_MAXSIZE=0 for a disabled row,
#                  which the header says takes precedence over the API.
# The six residency columns admit device memory held between requests, which
# execution_policy does not cover: that field admits the compute one request
# runs, and a process can hold a CUDA context, an acceleration structure and
# its buffers while running nothing. The two permissions are separate here
# because they are separately revocable -- a session that retains memory still
# takes the compute lease for each request and holds none between them -- and
# scripts/gpu-workloads.tsv remains the authority for the lease.
# residency         one-shot or bounded-resident. A one-shot row's runtime
#                   exits with its answer and releases every allocation with
#                   the process. A bounded-resident row's runtime keeps its
#                   CUDA context, OptiX context, module, pipeline, shader
#                   binding table and acceleration structure across the
#                   requests of one declared session.
# session_requests  the requests a session serves before it retires; 1 on a
#                   one-shot row, which is what such a process serves
# session_seconds   the wall seconds a session retires at, whichever bound
#                   arrives first
# idle_timeout_s    the interval with no request in hand that retires a
#                   session early; it has to be under session_seconds to fire
# residency_budget_mib
#                   the ceiling over the driver's reading for the whole
#                   process, which the supervisor takes at a moment it holds
#                   no lease and no request is in flight. It counts the CUDA
#                   context, the OptiX module and the pipeline, which are
#                   214 MiB on an RTX 4070 Ti before a request runs. A reading
#                   the probe cannot supply ends the session rather than
#                   passing as zero.
# application_budget_mib
#                   the ceiling over what the runtime asks cudaMalloc for,
#                   which it checks against a request's growth before it
#                   allocates. A row sizes it from the buffers max_rays
#                   admits plus an explicit scratch margin: a ray is 24 bytes
#                   and a result 8, so 1,048,576 rays occupy 32 MiB exactly,
#                   and 40 leaves 8 MiB beside the acceleration structure.
# The two ceilings are separate because they count different things and one
# number cannot bind both. Any value low enough to refuse a 32 MiB ray buffer
# is below the 214 MiB context, so the driver's reading fails first and no
# session starts; holding the driver's reading against the buffers instead
# would refuse every session the context alone. Separated, the application
# ceiling binds on the growth it can account for while the driver's reading
# keeps the allowance for the process.
# The four columns only a session has read n-a on a one-shot row.
# The two calibration rows carry bounds a measurement row is deliberately too
# generous to reach: geometry-cube-orbit-a-resident serves sixteen requests
# over three hundred seconds, so a run that measures what residency costs
# retires on the supervisor's word and never on its own.
# geometry-cube-orbit-a-appbudget declares 16 MiB of application allowance
# against a row whose max_rays needs 32, so 262,144 rays serve inside it and
# 1,048,576 are refused before a cudaMalloc runs. That pair is what shows the
# ceiling discriminating rather than failing everything. Reaching the idle
# interval, the request count and the wall bound is what proves destruction
# runs under the compute lease at each of them, and that needs a session
# small enough to end by itself inside a harness run.
# profile_id
